newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOE's Davies clarifies reported pound/mark remark.
newsitem.headline: BOE's Davies clarifies reported pound/mark remark.

text.p: Bank of England (BOE) Deputy Governor Howard Davies said on Wednesday that his reported remarks about the pound/mark rate reflected the view of financial markets and not the BOE, a British embassy spokesman in Tokyo told Reuters.
Earlier, Japanese news agency Jiji reported that Davies had said the pound was too high against the mark.

"Looking at the forward rate for the pound, it seems that the market is indicating that the pound's future value would level out or drop against the mark," the embassy spokesman quoted Davies as saying.
Davies was asked to clarify his remark, reported by Jiji, which was made at a news conference for the Japanese media.

Sterling rebounded against the mark in reaction to Davies's comments relayed by the embassy, rising to 2.7302/11 marks at 0929 GMT after falling to as low as around 2.7238 marks earlier on the Jiji report.
Davies is in Tokyo on a four-day official visit. He leaves for Britain on Thursday.
